1) DNA content of fibroblast cells can be used as a more precise basis for comparing metabolic responses to experimental manipulations than protein content, 2) fibroblast growth can be significantly stimulated by fructose, and 3) fibroblast metabolism can be significantly altered by fructose.
fructose is not as good a carbon source for growth as glucose, but it is a better carbon source for protein production.
the use of DNA as a basis for interpreting metabolic responses of human fibroblasts to experimental manipulations is a more precise approach than the use of protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a DNA basis for interpreting the effects of fructose on cell metabolism.
the effects of fructose on the metabolism of human fibroblasts, as determined by DNA measurements.
the development of a method for measuring DNA in human foreskin fibrobasts and the application of this procedure to the study of the effects of fructose on cell metabolism.

fructose is a poor substrate for growth of human fibroblasts and that fructose metabolism is associated with a reduction in N-acetyl-β-glucosaminase specific activity.
, although the effects of fructose and glucose on human fibroblasts are similar in terms of DNA and protein accumulation, there are significant differences in terms of enzyme activities.
fructose does not appear to be an optimal carbohydrate for human fibroblast growth, but that the metabolic effects of fructose on the cells are not as great as previously believed.

fructose is not a superior nutrient for the growth or metabolism of human fibroblasts.
fructose is a suitable substrate for human cell metabolism and that DNA measurement may be a useful basis for interpreting metabolic changes in cell populations.
